title: Claims cascade
headline: Each answer picks the next question: photo, catalogue, delivery, manual and history, in seconds.
developer: You are the after-sales claims triage system of Northwind Hogar, an online store for furniture, homeware and home electronics. Answer only from what the images and data show; if the evidence is unclear, reflect it in the probabilities.

prompts.entrega: Photo taken by the carrier when delivering the order:
prompts.json: Order, customer history and previous decisions for this claim:

nueva_foto.label: Ask for a new photo
nueva_foto.desc: The customer is asked for a sharp photo of the product, with no human involved.

fraude.label: Fraud review
fraude.desc: The product in the photo is not the one that was sold: it goes to the fraud team.

revision.label: Human review
revision.desc: Something doesn't add up or confidence is low: a person decides.

autoservicio.label: Guided fix
autoservicio.desc: The customer receives the steps from the manual. No return, no technician.

transportista.label: Replacement, charged to the carrier
transportista.desc: The product is replaced today and the cost is claimed from the carrier.

reposicion.label: Immediate replacement
reposicion.desc: A new product is shipped today.

foto_valida.label: Shows a product
foto_valida.instructions: Does the photo show a physical product (furniture, homeware or an appliance) that could be the subject of a claim? Answer no if it is a screenshot, a document, a person, a landscape or an image with no product.

nitidez.label: Sharpness
nitidez.instructions: Does the photo make it possible to assess the condition of the product?

levels.label: Blurry
levels.description: Shaken, out of focus or too dark: the product is barely recognisable and no details can be seen.

levels.label: Acceptable
levels.description: The product and its general condition can be recognised, although with little detail.

levels.label: Sharp
levels.description: In focus and well lit: the product's details can be seen.

route.reason: The photo does not show any product.
The photo is too blurry to assess the damage.

steps.title: Is it the product we sold?

otro_producto.label: Different product from the catalogue
otro_producto.instructions: Compare the product in the customer's photo with this catalogue photo of the item they were sold. Is it a different model: another kind of object or a clearly different design in shape, materials or colour? Damage, angle, lighting and background do not count as differences.

route.reason: The product in the photo is not the one that was sold.

danio_visible.label: Visible physical damage
danio_visible.instructions: Does the photo show physical damage to the product: breakage, a crack, a scratch, a dent or a detached part? A light or an indicator that is on is not physical damage.

tipo.label: Type of damage
tipo.instructions: What type of physical damage can be seen on the product?

rotura.label: Breakage
rotura.description: Broken parts, fragments or shattered glass.

grieta.label: Crack
grieta.description: A fissure or crack, including a cracked screen.

aranazo.label: Scratch
aranazo.description: Scratches or scuffs on the surface.

ninguno.label: None
ninguno.description: No physical damage can be seen.

gravedad.label: Severity
gravedad.instructions: How does the damage affect the use of the product?

levels.label: Minor
levels.description: Cosmetic damage: the product works normally.

levels.label: Moderate
levels.description: Affects appearance or use, but the product still works.

levels.label: Unusable
levels.description: The product cannot be used or is dangerous to use.

relato_cuadra.label: Account matches the photo
relato_cuadra.instructions: Is what the customer says consistent with what the photo shows? A functional fault does not always show in a photo: it is enough that the photo does not contradict the account. Answer no if the customer describes damage or a product that does not appear in the photo.

route.reason: The customer's account does not match the photo.
No visible physical damage: possible functional fault.

embalaje_danado.label: Packaging damaged on delivery
embalaje_danado.instructions: This is the photo the carrier took when delivering the order. Is the box or packaging crushed, torn, open, wet or dented?

route.reason: The parcel arrived damaged: the carrier is liable.

averia.label: Fault according to the manual
averia.instructions: Based on the technical manual and what the customer says, what is the most likely fault?

cepillo_atascado.label: Jammed brush
cepillo_atascado.description: Hair or threads tangled in the main brush or the side brushes.

bateria.label: Battery
bateria.description: The battery does not charge or runs out very quickly.

sensores_sucios.label: Dirty sensors
sensores_sucios.description: Cliff or obstacle sensors are dirty or covered.

base_carga.label: Charging dock
base_carga.description: The robot cannot find the dock or does not charge on it.

motor.label: Motor
motor.description: Abnormal noise, burning smell or the motor does not turn.

desconocida.label: Unknown
desconocida.description: The symptoms do not match any fault in the manual.

autoservicio.label: Customer can fix it
autoservicio.instructions: According to the manual, can the customer fix this fault by following the maintenance steps, without special tools and without opening the device?

route.reason: The manual has the fix: the steps are sent to the customer.

riesgo.label: Abuse risk
riesgo.instructions: Given the order data, the customer's history and the previous decisions on this claim, what is the risk of abuse or fraud in approving the replacement without human review?

levels.label: Low
levels.description: Good history and a consistent, on-time claim.

levels.label: Medium
levels.description: An isolated warning sign, such as a recent previous claim.

levels.label: High
levels.description: Abuse pattern: several recent claims or returns, a late claim or data that doesn't add up.

route.reason: Damage confirmed, intact delivery and a reliable customer.

items.text: Three of the six glasses arrived broken. The box was crushed on one side and the courier was in a big hurry.
When I unpacked the table I found a long scratch on the top. The box was perfect, so it must have left the warehouse like that.
Since yesterday the robot stops a few minutes after starting and a red light blinks. I have a very hairy dog, not sure if that matters.
The coffee machine leaks water from the bottom every time I use it. Here's a photo.
The lamp arrived broken: the shade is bent and the bulb is shattered. I want a full refund.
The monitor has a huge crack in the screen from the moment I took it out of the box. I want a new one.

notes.reto: Every after-sales claim with a photo needs someone to look at the image, check it is the product sold, assess the damage and review the delivery and the customer's history. That is about **8 minutes per case**, and the customer waits for days.
notes.solucion: A **decision cascade**: each step is a call to the OpenAI Decisions API with closed questions, and its answers pick the next step. Image steps (customer photo, catalogue, delivery) alternate with text-only steps (technical manual, history as JSON), plus a deterministic business rule.
notes.paradigma: You don't need a generative agent to "reason" through each case: an **explicit, auditable decision tree** whose nodes return calibrated probabilities is enough. Whatever falls below the confidence threshold goes to a person; the rest is resolved automatically, in seconds and for cents.
